hardware.gpu: AMD Radeon Pro 5500M 4 GiB (unused: runner reported 100% CPU)

bandwidth.note: of probe, NumPy STREAM add kernel. An independent C pthread implementation measured 20.4 GB/s at 8 threads, confirming the figure is not a NumPy artefact.

runs.note: Different architecture entirely: 48 state-space layers among 64, plus a vision encoder and an MTP head excluded from the active set. Load took 48s and the 17.4 GB file nearly fills 32 GB of RAM, which may explain the slightly lower figure.

conclusion.spread: 2.0% across a 3.5x range of model sizes
conclusion.reasoning: Three models spanning 4.7-16.2 GB of active weight, across two unrelated architectures, imply the same read bandwidth to within 2%. That is the signature of a bandwidth-bound process and confirms tok/s = bandwidth / active_bytes_per_token. The factor above 1.0 reflects that weight streaming is pure sequential read, while the STREAM add kernel pays for writes and read-for-ownership.
